PRIMARY CARE NOTE   Date: 2026-07-10
45M, ambulatory visit for an annual check-up.

S:
Patient presents for a routine check-up. He reports feeling generally well, with occasional wheezing on exertion and with dust exposure that responds to his reliever. Diet is high in sugary drinks and takeout, which was discussed. He works as an electrician. Sister with schizophrenia. Mother with rheumatoid arthritis. Sleep is adequate and appetite is good. Lives with his spouse and children. Never smoker, occasional alcohol on weekends.

O:
BP 122/78, HR 70, RR 14, Temp 98.1 F, SpO2 98% on room air. Weight 192 lb, BMI 28.
General: well appearing, in no acute distress.
HEENT: nasal mucosa normal, oropharynx clear.
CV: regular rate and rhythm, no murmur.
Lungs: clear to auscultation bilaterally at rest.
Abdomen: soft, nontender.
Extremities: no edema, joints without swelling.
Labs (prior week): A1c 6.0%, lipid panel within goal, basic metabolic panel within normal limits.

A/P:
1. Asthma, uncomplicated, using inhaler as needed. Continue short-acting reliever before exertion; inhaler technique reviewed and adequate. Provided a written action plan and advised a dust mask at work.
2. Prediabetes, counseled on diet and exercise. Reviewed reducing sugary drinks, portion control, and adding regular walks. Recheck A1c in 6 months.
3. Family history: reviewed relevant family history with patient and discussed age-appropriate screening and reassurance.
4. Health maintenance: colorectal screening discussed and scheduled. Influenza vaccine offered in the fall. Encouraged regular physical activity and adequate hydration.

Return in 12 months for the next wellness visit, sooner if breathing or new symptoms develop.
